newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinians disappointed with U.S. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians disappointed with U.S. envoy.

text.p: Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said on Saturday the Palestinians were disappointed that U.S. envoy Dennis Ross had failed to blame Israel for obstructing progress towards an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
Ross returned to the United States earlier this week after days trying to bridge the gap between Israel and the Palestinians on the redeployment in the West Bank town.

"The Palestinians had hoped from the United States, by virtue of the fact that it took part in the negotiations, that Dennis Ross would at least announce which was the party responsible for obstructing implementation of the agreement and which was the party trying to change the agreement signed," Erekat said.

The Palestinians insist Israel must carry out the Hebron agreement it signed more than a year ago. The rightwing Israeli government, which came to power after the agreement was signed, wants to make amendments on security grounds.
Erekat was speaking at the Egyptian foreign ministry after talks with Nabil Fahmi, a senior political adviser to Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
Erekat said he and his delegation also met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Saturday to give him a message from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat. Arafat saw Mubarak in Cairo on Friday.

"This Israeli government...is acting, to be quite frank, against everything that was agreed and against the whole peace process, not only on the Palestinian track but also on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," Erekat said.

"It has been carrying out campaigns of widespread deception since the moment the talks started, either by making accusations against the Palestinian side or by inventing problems with Egypt and the states of the region generally," he added.
